citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance
reason: Same rent-control law/category as BER-RENT-01. This record mainly describes coverage/exemptions for Berkeley’s rent ordinance, while BER-RENT-01 better states the main operative rent-increase requirement. Coverage/exemption provisions are part of the same law and should be merged into one kept record per law per category.

citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance; Ellis Implementation Ordinance
reason: Relocation assistance for owner move-in and Ellis evictions is part of Berkeley's just-cause eviction regime and annual adjustment of payment amounts. Under the duplicate rule, relocation/implementation provisions of the same law should be merged into the main just-cause record.

This ordinance requires a tenant-rights/resources notice and city filing when serving a notice to quit or non-renewal, but it expressly does not limit the grounds for eviction or non-renewal. In just_cause_eviction, notice provisions are operative only when part of a just-cause regime; here it is a procedural notice tied to eviction, not a cause limitation.

This record mainly states that application screening fees are not security deposits and are governed by the separate application-screening-fee statute; it does not itself impose an operative security-deposit rule.

Main operative subject is application screening fee caps and procedures, not screening restrictions such as criminal-history or source-of-income limits. Timing/availability conditions here are part of the fee statute and are better kept in application_screening_fees.

citation: San Francisco Rent Board Current Rates, including Rent Increase, Relocation, Sec. Deposit
reason: This record gives only the annual interest rate on security deposits and expressly lacks any maximum deposit amount; it does not state an operative security-deposit cap or comparable rule for this category.
